data.title: Paid Launches Token Issuance Feature on Pons
data.description: Paid said on X that it has launched token issuance functionality on Pons. According to ChainCatcher, 80% of fees will be sent to X users via X Money, while 20% will be converted into SOL to buy back PAID tokens. Issuers can add an X handle to the project description to send fees through X Money.

data.title: Polymarket Bitcoin September 19 Breakout Bet Sees Sharp Swing in 82,000 Yes Odds
data.description: Catcher Predict monitoring showed that the "Yes" option for the "82,000" submarket in Polymarket's "Bitcoin breaks through on September 19" event rose sharply from 7% one hour earlier to 24.1% at the time of reporting. According to ChainCatcher, the move reflected a 17.1 percentage point swing and came amid attention to possible breaking news impacts.

data.title: Iran Says It Set Negotiating Conditions for the U.S. Through Qatar and Pakistan
data.description: According to Sina Finance, Iran's Supreme National Security Council Secretary Mohsen Rezaei said on Saturday that Iran has set negotiating conditions for the U.S. through mediators in Qatar and Pakistan: a complete end to fighting on all fronts, the release of seized Iranian assets, and the lifting of the naval blockade. Rezaei said Tehran remains in contact with the Qatari mediator, who has conveyed Iran's conditions to the U.S. in an effort to end the war, and is now waiting for a response from U.S. President Donald Trump.

data.title: Charles Hoskinson Says Crypto Will “Eat” AI Over The Next 5 To 10 Years
data.description:
Cardano founder Charles Hoskinson said blockchain will eventually absorb AI, arguing that cryptocurrencies will “eat” AI over the next 5 to 10 years as data center spending outpaces grid capacity and model training costs squeeze profitability. according to BeInCrypto, he said blockchains could solve payments, alignment and data provenance, while also supporting distributed training and local AI models.

Hoskinson also said the CLARITY Act may not pass Congress until 2029, blaming Trump administration missteps and the bill’s association with Trump-branded tokens.

data.title: New York City Forms 36-Person Data Bureau to Probe Consumer Violations
data.description:
New York City is creating a 36-person bureau of data scientists, technologists and economists to review company records for possible violations involving pricing, wages and other consumer and worker protections, according to Bloomberg.

NYC Consumer and Worker Protection Commissioner Sam Levine said on Bloomberg This Weekend that the unit is meant to give the city technical expertise to enforce existing laws as algorithms and AI play a growing role in how companies set prices and compensation.

data.title: Visa Moves to Stop Memecoin Purchases Being Classified as Digital Media
data.description: Visa is moving to stop crypto payment processors from categorizing memecoin purchases as digital media, according to a Friday report from Crypto in America. According to NS3.AI, the classification had allowed users to buy memecoins with credit cards and earn ordinary points or cash back. The processors have an expected grace period ending next week, after which memecoin purchases would be processed as typical cryptocurrency transactions subject to Visa's restrictions.

data.title: GEOPOLITICS | Hormuz Oil, LNG Shipments Reach Six-Month High, US Commander Says
data.description:
Oil and liquefied natural gas shipments through the Strait of Hormuz over the past two weeks reached their highest level in six months, according to Bloomberg.

A regional US commander said the increase suggests US naval protection and mine clearance efforts are "paying off."

data.title: Utah Governor Cox Calls for Healthier Political Conflict
data.description:
Utah Governor Spencer Cox told Bloomberg This Weekend that Americans need more substantive disagreement without the contempt he says is fueling polarization, damaged relationships and political violence, according to Bloomberg.

In his new book, Off Ramp, Cox calls for healthier political conflict and stronger local connections, and says policymakers need more expertise to address emerging challenges such as AI.

data.title: Grayscale's ZCSH Files 3-for-1 Forward Share Split as Zcash Rises
data.description: Grayscale's ZCSH Zcash ETF has filed for a 3-for-1 forward share split to lower its per-share price as ZEC's value has surged. According to NS3.AI, shareholders of record at the close of trading on Sept. 28 will receive two additional shares for each share held, and split-adjusted trading is scheduled to begin before market open on Sept. 30.

data.title: Genius.fun Launches on BNB Chain and Reports $303,100 in Buybacks
data.description: Genius.fun launched on BNB Chain on September 17 and allows creators to transfer tokenized stocks such as bSTOCKS into an ownerless foundation and unwrap them in an attempt to exercise related equity rights off-chain. According to Odaily, the platform has repurchased $303,100 worth of tokens, and GSTOCK has the highest market value among its issued tokens at $6.9 million after reaching $10 million after launch. GSTOCK uses BNCB, the on-chain token of BNB treasury company BNC, as its pool pairing.

data.title: Ares Considers Minority Stake in Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners
data.description:
Ares Management Corp. is exploring a purchase of a minority stake in Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners, according to Bloomberg.

The potential deal would mark the latest high-profile expansion by the private markets firm into the infrastructure sector.

data.title: STOCKS | SpaceX Weight in Nasdaq 100 to Rise to 2.82%
data.description:
SpaceX's weight in the Nasdaq 100 index will rise to 2.82% when the index's quarterly rebalancing takes effect next Monday, up from about 1.28% now. According to Sina Finance, the final figure, calculated from Friday's closing price, matches the preliminary weight previously announced by the index compiler.

SpaceX's weight has been relatively low since it was added to the index in July, when most of the company's shares were still locked up and unavailable for public trading. Even after Nasdaq changed its rules to allow newly listed large-cap stocks to enter the index more quickly and removed the requirement that at least 10% of a company's shares be freely tradable, that factor still weighed on its index weight.

The expected increase will begin to narrow that gap. By market capitalization, SpaceX is the seventh-largest company in the Nasdaq 100, with a market value above $2 trillion, but by index weight it does not even rank in the top 20.

The higher weight matters because passive funds tied to the benchmark must adjust their holdings accordingly. Those funds include the $482 billion Invesco QQQ Trust Series 1, known as QQQ, one of the largest ETFs. More than 200 investment products worldwide track the Nasdaq 100, with assets under management exceeding $800 billion.

The Nasdaq 100 tracks large nonfinancial companies listed on the Nasdaq market. There is no minimum market-cap requirement for inclusion, but companies must have average daily trading volume of at least 200,000 shares and meet other conditions.

Edward Yin of Macquarie Group said recent index rebalancing events have taken on greater significance amid multiple market drivers. He said the adjustment is taking place against a more volatile macro backdrop, citing geopolitical tensions involving Iran, persistent inflation concerns, renewed tariff uncertainty, interest-rate moves, and continued volatility in artificial intelligence and technology stocks.

data.title: Circle's Arc Launches Facilitator Service for x402 Developer Payments
data.description: Circle's Arc public blockchain has launched agent payments through its Facilitator Service. According to Odaily, the service provides x402 developers with a hosted access path that accepts USDC and supports on-chain settlement on Arc, Base, and Polygon, without requiring a Relayer key or a separate gas fee wallet.

data.title: AI TRENDS | CoinMarketCap’s Alice Liu Says Crypto AI Capital Is Concentrating in Fewer Tokens
data.description: Crypto’s AI-token market is becoming more selective, with capital flowing into a small group of projects while hundreds of AI-labeled tokens struggle to attract meaningful participation. According to NS3.AI, CoinMarketCap’s Alice Liu said the category includes about 945 tokens worth $18.5 billion in total, but fewer than one in 10 meet both a $20 million market-cap threshold and $1 million in daily trading volume. Liu expects AI’s share of crypto capital to grow while concentrating in perhaps a dozen or two names.

data.title: Blink Says Attackers Accessed Small Number of Custodial Accounts and Withdrew Funds
data.description: Bitcoin News posted on X that attackers accessed a small number of Blink custodial accounts and withdrew funds. According to Odaily, Blink said most funds remain safe, non-custodial wallets were not affected, and it has not confirmed whether the Bitcoin payment protocol Spark, which supports several Lightning Network wallets, was the source of the security incident.

data.title: SEC Issues Innovation Exemption for On-Chain Secondary Trading of Tokenized Stocks
data.description:
Galaxy’s head of research said on X that the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission has issued an "innovation exemption" to create a path for on-chain secondary trading of tokenized stocks. According to Odaily, the exemption will run from September 17, 2026, to September 17, 2031, and will apply to certain tokenized securities trading venues that offer permissioned automated market makers and liquidity pools.

The venues must be deployed on public, permissionless blockchains, but trading will be limited to verified or authorized participants. Eligible tokens must correspond to actual U.S. National Market System stocks and grant the same shareholder rights as traditional shares. The exemption does not cover primary issuance, synthetic exposure, or products that do not carry legal or beneficial rights to the underlying stock. Galaxy said it is studying next steps for enabling on-chain secondary trading of GLXY.

data.title: Hut 8 Co-Founder Warns AI Growth Could Pose Systemic Risks
data.description:
Hut 8 co-founder Marc van der Chijs warned in a CoinDesk interview that intense competition between companies and nations is accelerating artificial intelligence development beyond human control, creating potential systemic risks for financial systems and critical infrastructure. According to ChainCatcher, he said the situation has already been lost to control and that systemic damage or catastrophic failure may be nearly unavoidable before real international guardrails are established.

Van der Chijs said AI and robotics could eventually replace 90% to 95% of existing jobs and sharply reduce the cost of goods and services, forcing governments to seek new revenue sources such as taxes on robots or AI use. He also said AI could expose vulnerabilities in traditional banking software and weaken confidence in institutions that rely on interconnected systems. In crypto, he argued that businesses built around Bitcoin, such as exchanges, may be more vulnerable than the underlying network itself.

He said he previously sold a large amount of Bitcoin to invest in AI and believes capital shifting into AI helped prevent Bitcoin from reaching his earlier $200,000 to $250,000 target. He is now reinvesting some AI profits into crypto assets through exchange-traded funds. Van der Chijs said he still views Bitcoin as the only asset worth holding for life and called Hut 8's move into AI data centers the best decision it has ever made.

data.title: Moody’s Lowers Mozambique Further Into Junk on Eurobond Restructuring Risk
data.description: Moody’s Ratings cut Mozambique’s credit assessment deeper into junk, citing increased risk that the gas-rich southeast African nation will restructure its sole eurobond, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: SAVE Borrowers Face Higher Student Loan Bills as Exit Deadline Nears
data.description:
According to CNBC, many federal student loan borrowers could see their monthly payments double or triple in the coming weeks if they do not leave the now-defunct Saving on a Valuable Education, or SAVE, repayment plan. The Trump administration told borrowers earlier this year that they would have about 90 days to move to another program, and for some borrowers that window began July 1, making the earliest deadline Sept. 29.

Servicers are sending notices in waves, so many borrowers have more time. More than 6.9 million borrowers were still enrolled in SAVE as of March, with an average debt of about $55,000, according to an analysis by higher education expert Mark Kantrowitz. If borrowers do not choose another repayment plan within 90 days of notification, they will be moved into either the Standard Repayment Plan or the new Tiered Standard Plan, which launched July 1. Kantrowitz said payments for some borrowers could double or triple.

The Biden administration-era SAVE plan offered very low monthly payments, but it was overturned by Republican-led legal challenges and legislation. Many enrollees have not made a payment in more than two years while lawsuits played out, and their balances have grown with interest. Borrowers can apply for another income-driven repayment plan through studentaid.gov or their servicer's website, but the Education Department is still working through a backlog of more than 530,000 pending income-driven repayment applications as of the end of April, according to a May court filing.

A new income-driven option, the Repayment Assistance Plan, or RAP, launched in July and caps monthly payments at 1% to 10% of earnings, with loan forgiveness after 30 years. An analysis provided to CNBC by student loan advisory platform Summer found that a two-person household earning just over $50,000 with $60,000 in student debt at a 6.8% interest rate would owe $690 a month under the 10-year Standard Repayment Plan, compared with $158 under RAP.

data.title: AI | MBA Programs Adapt as Stanford Keeps Top Spot in Bloomberg Businessweek Rankings
data.description:
Stanford Graduate School of Business remained No. 1 in Bloomberg Businessweek’s US MBA rankings, with strong marks in compensation, networking and entrepreneurship, according to Bloomberg.

Bloomberg Businessweek Senior Editor Dimitra Kessenides said business schools are also testing AI in teaching, case studies and career preparation as they work to give graduates the skills employers increasingly expect.
